# Test fixtures

- `readsb-sample.jsonl`: synthetic readsb JSON-port output, generated by
  `gen_readsb_jsonl.py` (see its docstring).
- `raw/`: real receiver captures, used by `test_rawtools.sh` and handy for
  `skycue-rawplay`. They are third-party data under their own
  licences: fetched by `scripts/fixtures/fetch-test-captures.sh`, not in the repository
  and not distributed in releases. The captures are git-ignored; the one committed
  file is the derived `modes-120s.golden.jsonl.gz` (below).
- `fisb/`: FIS-B uplink test data (fisb-decode's `tg30.978`, fetched, and
  `received-with-uplinks.jsonl` and `received-tg30.jsonl`, regenerated from the
  fetched files by `fisb/gen_received_with_uplinks.py` and
  `fisb/gen_received_tg30.py`), used by the `test_fisb_*` tests; origin,
  licence and contents in `fisb/README.md`. `pireps-synthetic.txt` is
  hand-written and committed.
- `pingstation/`: pingStation 3 JSON fixtures, all generated by the project's
  own simulator or written by hand: `traffic-1090.json`, `status.json`,
  `status-curly-quotes.json` (generated by `gen.sh`) and `uat-detail.json`
  (hand-written); see `pingstation/README.md`.
- `config-copy.toml`: exactly what the web Config tab's "Copy as text"
  (`app_pure.js` `configText`) writes for the values in `tests/js`'s
  `CFG_COPY`, one key per kind of value and escape; the node test checks the
  text, `test_config` parses it with `parseConfigText` and skycued reads it
  as a config. Hand-written; regenerate it if `configText` changes.
- `icao_class_cases.json`: cases for the page's address country, military
  block, callsign kind and track class rules (`app_pure.js`), run by
  `tests/js/app_pure.test.js` against the page and by `test_icao_class` against
  the daemon's copy (`skycued/src/icao_class.cpp`). Hand-written; the JS is the
  source of truth.

## Fetching the third-party captures

These files are not in the repository. Without them the test cases that read
them are skipped (the skip message names the file).

`scripts/fixtures/fetch-test-captures.sh [--cache DIR] [--fixtures DIR] [--offline]`
downloads the captures below from their upstream repositories (or, for OpenSky
and Zenodo, their data hosts) at pinned URLs, checks their SHA-256 values and installs
`raw/modes-120s.csv.gz`, `raw/uat-sample.txt.gz`, `raw/stratux-uat-2015.log.gz`,
`raw/stratux-uat-2015b.log.gz`,
`fisb/tg30.978`, `raw/pymodes-*.csv`, `raw/dump1090-modes1.bin` and `opensky/*/`
(`iq/porto-awec2026/` only with `SKYCUE_FETCH_IQ=1`), then
regenerates `fisb/received-with-uplinks.jsonl` and `fisb/received-tg30.jsonl`
with the generators in `fisb/`. These paths are git-ignored. The pins are in
one block in the script (`# --- pins ---`). Pinned upstream commits (resolved
2026-11-05; each file's SHA-256 at that commit equals the copy recorded below):

| Capture | Repository | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| modes | junzis/pyModeS | `487cfd6139ecea10a833afea2e58f631dc875702` |
| uat sample | flightaware/dump978 | `f40aa9a0d2d0a0067c0c628b44ba316f7049b8ce` |
| stratux log | cyoung/stratux | `1a0d1ca9e94d1c98ae1f4305e073fdd6b5a810be` |
| stratux log b | stratux/stratux | `240f7825991eed62ff3dcd8bf7465e597df00442` (the commit that added the file; it is absent at the commit above) |
| tg30 | rand-projects/fisb-decode | `c3d3b0473429336b1a98672b2e8b276c24d49765` |
| pyModeS tests/data | junzis/pyModeS | `487cfd6139ecea10a833afea2e58f631dc875702` |
| modes1.bin | MalcolmRobb/dump1090 | `bff92c4ad772a0a8d433f788d39dae97e00e4dbe` |

## raw/modes-120s.csv.gz

- Origin: https://github.com/junzis/pyModeS, file
  `scripts/data/airsquitter_2026-07-13_120s.csv.gz` (renamed here).
- Licence: GPL-3.0 (the pyModeS repository's licence).
- Content: 120 s of 1090 MHz Mode S traffic (European, 2026-07-13), 176,612
  messages (118,059 short, 14 hex digits; 58,553 long, 28 hex digits); readsb
  positions 182 aircraft from it at speed 1.
- Line format: `epoch_seconds.fraction,HEX`, no header, gzip-compressed.
  First line: `1783963099.005369,5F406A936F50F0`.
- Decoding positions needs a receiver location near the traffic, e.g.
  `--lat 52.0 --lon 4.5 --max-range 500` for readsb.
- sha256: `fa433eb8dc2ec9cf6ebd40c1bf0a095ae753960d5e8c42ae6da15cc28eb3baea`

## raw/modes-120s.golden.jsonl.gz

Provenance: derived facts (ICAO addresses, positions, identity fields, counts)
computed by readsb 3.16.21 (regenerated 2026-11-09, now also with the Comm-B, TC29 and airspeed fields) from the pyModeS-hosted capture; no capture bytes are included.

What readsb 3.16.21 makes of `raw/modes-120s.csv.gz`, committed (about 13 KB; the
capture itself is not) so `decode_golden` can compare the 1090 decoder with it. It is
aircraft data only: one JSON object per address, sorted by hex, with `positions` (the
number of changes of readsb's reported position), `second` and `last` position
(`t`, `lat`, `lon`), and, from the line that carried the last position, `alt_baro`,
`gs`, `track`, `baro_rate`, `geom_rate`, `heading_mag_deg`, `heading_true_deg`, `ias_kt`, `tas_kt`, `mach`, `roll_deg`,
`track_rate_dps`, `sel_alt_ft`, `sel_alt_fms_ft`, `qnh_mb`, `sel_heading_deg`, `nav_modes` (readsb's `mag_heading`, `true_heading`,
`ias`, `tas`, `mach`, `roll`, `track_rate`, `nav_*`, under skycued's names), `flight`, `category`, `squawk`, `nic`, `nac_p`
where readsb had them. `gen_raw_golden.sh READSB RAWPLAY CSV_GZ OUT_GZ` makes it: it
starts readsb without `--lat`/`--lon` (global CPR decoding only, as the test feeds
the decoder) with a raw input port and a JSON output port that includes aircraft
without positions, plays the capture in with `skycue-rawplay --speed 1` (real
time, about two minutes; faster playback breaks readsb's position speed check, which
uses its own clock), collects the JSON lines and reduces them with
`gen_raw_golden.py` (Python 3 standard library only). Both binaries are arguments.
skycued decodes the same Comm-B and TC29 content; `heading_true_deg` is reported but not gated (readsb derives
it from a declination model).

## raw/uat-sample.txt.gz

- Origin: https://github.com/flightaware/dump978, file `sample-data.txt.gz`
  (renamed here).
- Licence: BSD-2-Clause (the dump978 repository's licence).
- Content: 1,143 dump978 raw UAT messages: 439 downlink, 704 uplink.
- Line format: `-<hex>;` (downlink) or `+<hex>;` (uplink), no timestamps,
  gzip-compressed. skycue-rawplay paces such files at 10 lines/s.
  First line: `-00a66ef135445d525a0c0519119021204800;`.
- sha256: `86248797f4334a134ccf4349dabf800a7054d698828b88838dc7950a99f9ae24`

## raw/uat-sample.golden.jsonl.gz

- Made by `gen_uat_golden.sh DUMP978 IQGEN SAMPLE_GZ OUT_GZ` from the downlink
  lines of `uat-sample.txt.gz`: `skycue-iqgen uat` modulates them to a temporary
  CU8 file (deleted on exit, about 80 KB per frame), dump978-fa (from the
  flightaware/dump978 repository, at the commit pinned above for the uat sample, `f40aa9a0d2d0a0067c0c628b44ba316f7049b8ce`) demodulates it with `--raw-stdout
  --json-stdout`, and `gen_uat_golden.py` pairs each raw line with the JSON
  object of the same `received_at`. Both binaries are arguments; nothing in the
  repository knows where they live. The script fails on a JSON key it does not
  know and on more than 5 % of downlinks without JSON.
- Content: one object per downlink (439 of 439 paired), keys `hex`, `address`,
  `qualifier`, `ag`, `lat`, `lon`, `alt_baro`, `alt_geom`, `gs`, `track`,
  `vrate`, `vrate_src`, `callsign`, `squawk` (dump978-fa's `flightplan_id`),
  `category`, `emergency`, `nic`, `nac_p`; keys the tool did not print are absent.
- Coverage: every frame is airborne; qualifiers `adsb_icao`, `tisb_icao`,
  `tisb_trackfile`; emitter categories A0-A2; emergency always `none`.
  Surface frames come from the Stratux golden below.
- Licence: derived from `uat-sample.txt.gz` (frames and the decoded values of them), so
  BSD-2-Clause as for the dump978 repository's sample data.
- Used by `tests/test_decode_uat_golden.cpp` (ctest `decode_uat_golden`).
- Also used by `tests/test_decode_differential_uat.sh` (ctest `decode_differential_uat`),
  the live end-to-end twin: skycue-rawplay replays `uat-sample.txt.gz` at speed 1 into
  skycued (`inputs.decoder = "skycued"`, a `uat_raw` input), the recorded received stream is
  reduced per address (`reduce_received.py --uat`), the golden the same way
  (`--uat-golden`; positions more than 300 NM from the test's receiver, one aircraft, are left
  out because the decoder rejects them), and `compare_tracks.py --uat` compares. With
  `SKYCUE_DUMP978` set to a dump978-fa executable the golden is also regenerated fresh
  and ours is compared with that.

## raw/uat-stratux.golden.jsonl.gz

- The same pipeline on the downlinks of `stratux-uat-2015.log.gz`: the generator
  strips the leading `TIMESTAMP,` of each `TIMESTAMP,-HEX;rs=N;` line and skips
  uplinks and `START,` lines. One CU8 file for all 3,760 frames (about 310 MB,
  deleted on exit); the run takes about 15 s.
- Content: 3,760 of 3,760 downlinks paired. 3,209 airborne, 551 surface (426 with
  track type 1 and a track, 125 with type 0 and none); 3,576 `tisb_trackfile`
  and 184 `adsb_icao`; categories A0 and A1 only; emergency always `none`;
  every frame has a position; adds `aircraft_size` (read, not kept) on surface
  frames.
- Not covered: track types 2 and 3, categories above A1, emergency values other
  than `none`, frames without a position.
- Licence: derived from `stratux-uat-2015.log.gz` (frames and the decoded values of
  them), so BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2015 Christopher Young, as for the stratux
  repository (the licence text is under `raw/stratux-uat-2015.log.gz` below).

## raw/uat-stratux-b.golden.jsonl.gz

- The same pipeline on the downlinks of `stratux-uat-2015b.log.gz`: 303 of 303
  paired (ratio 1.00), all airborne `tisb_trackfile`, category A0, emergency
  `none`, every frame positioned. It adds no coverage the other two goldens lack.
- Licence: derived from `stratux-uat-2015b.log.gz`, so BSD-3-Clause, Copyright
  (c) 2015 Christopher Young, as for the stratux repository.

## raw/uat-synthetic.golden.jsonl.gz and raw/uat-synthetic.expect.jsonl.gz

- Made by `gen_uat_synthetic.sh DUMP978 IQGEN OUT_GZ EXPECT_GZ [UAT_SYNTH]`: the test
  helper `uat_synth` (built from `tests/uat_synth.cpp` and `tests/uat_test_support.hpp`'s
  `encodeUat`) prints the 109 frames of the matrix and writes the values built into each;
  `gen_uat_golden.sh` then runs the frames through `skycue-iqgen` and dump978-fa as for the
  goldens above (temporary CU8, about 9 MB, deleted on exit). The `.golden` file has the
  tool's decode (same keys as the other goldens, plus `mag_heading` and `true_heading` for
  ground track types 2 and 3), the `.expect` file one object per frame, keyed by `hex`, with
  `row`, `group` and the built-in values in the same key names (a key is absent where the row
  builds "not available"). 109 of 109 paired.
- Content: emitter categories 0..39, emergency codes 0..7, ground state vectors with track
  types 0..3 and speed not available, a frame without a position, N/S or E/W velocity not
  available, a supersonic one, vertical rate (baro and geometric, up and down, not
  available), a squawk and a call sign, secondary altitude present and absent with a
  barometric and a geometric primary, address qualifiers 0..6, positions near the corners,
  the origin and the equator/meridian, altitudes -1000, 0 and 101,350 ft, NIC 0..11, NACp 0..11.
  Every frame is made by us, so there is no third-party content and no licence beyond this repository's.
- Used by `tests/test_decode_uat_synthetic.cpp` (ctest `decode_uat_synthetic`).

## raw/stratux-uat-2015.log.gz

- Origin: https://github.com/cyoung/stratux, file
  `test-data/cyoung-09062015-noproblem-stratux-uat.log` at commit
  `1a0d1ca9e94d1c98ae1f4305e073fdd6b5a810be` (renamed here, content
  unchanged, compressed with `gzip -9n`); downloaded 2026-11-02.
- Licence: BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2015 Christopher Young (the stratux
  repository's `LICENSE` at that commit, full text below).
- Content: 22,556 lines: 11,276 UAT messages (7,516 uplink, all 432 bytes;
  3,760 downlink, 107 short of 18 bytes and 3,653 long of 34 bytes; none of
  a wrong length), each followed by a blank line, and 4 `START,<date>`
  session header lines. Two recording sessions: offsets 162.698 s to
  2507.803 s (8,125 messages, 2,345 s), then, after the header on line
  16,253, from 65.807 s again to 2205.878 s (3,151 messages, 2,140 s).
- Line format: `<ns>,<+|->HEX;[rs=N;]`: `<ns>` a nanosecond offset from an
  arbitrary start, then a dump978 raw line (`rs=` on 7,245 of them).
  skycue-rawplay strips the offset and paces by it; skycue-iqgen times
  frames by it. A `START` line or a backward offset begins a new session:
  both tools play the sessions in file order, never interleaved, each one
  1 s after the previous session's last message with its own spacing kept
  (skycued::StratuxClock). Here session 2 follows at 2346.105 s from the
  first message. Both skip and count the `START` lines.
  First line: `START,Wed Sep 2 04:23:37 +0000 UTC 2015`; first message:
  `162698355928,-0b2b4a513c417b8875f40d9610f227401105c4e6c4e6c40a32700300000000000000;rs=4;`.
- sha256: `53fc80938c55d777ef85929fbaef519a7ccfa41ecb37c6e23aa773daebe5d588`
  (the uncompressed log:
  `fd4b376c7d90fe92dd1f9d5f2f8d11a19deb81ea3dc68e9b6e10f091e33d73f5`)

## raw/pymodes-adsb.csv, raw/pymodes-commb-df20.csv, raw/pymodes-commb-df21.csv

- Origin: https://github.com/junzis/pyModeS, files `tests/data/sample_data_adsb.csv`,
  `sample_data_commb_df20.csv` and `sample_data_commb_df21.csv` at commit
  `487cfd6139ecea10a833afea2e58f631dc875702` (renamed here, content unchanged).
- Licence: GPL-3.0 (the pyModeS repository's licence; no separate data licence). Fetched
  only, never committed or distributed in releases, like `modes-120s.csv.gz`.
- Content: `pymodes-adsb.csv`: 2,000 DF17 frames over 730 s from 2016-03-15 (1,032
  addresses; type codes 11 position 937, 19 velocity 965, 4 identification 98; the
  origin of the capture is not stated). `pymodes-commb-df20.csv` and `-df21.csv`: 5,000 DF20
  and 5,000 DF21 Comm-B replies each (189 and 158 addresses), from 2017-05-21, about 26
  s and 61 s; the Comm-B payloads (BDS 4,0, 5,0, 6,0 and others) are what makes
  them useful, as ADS-B captures hold none.
- Line format: `epoch,"HEX","icao",typecode` (adsb) and `epoch,ICAO,HEX` (commb); epoch
  in whole seconds, many frames share one second; the commb files start with a UTF-8
  byte order mark. Sizes 107,902 and 240,003 bytes each.
- Use: hand-run with a loop that strips the columns; no test reads them yet. They cover
  the DF20/21 path (altitude, identity code, no ADS-B content) that the 120 s capture
  barely touches.
- sha256: `7534e8186adec1aa44589c27d6059d0cde102c12d7e77c2584041f33afb99d9f` (adsb),
  `4c3ac03dd47c1280a9b98fb7e951fa52afa33597421f25a8068fd23f12195a08` (df20),

## opensky/

- Origin: the OpenSky Network sample bucket, `https://s3.opensky-network.org/data-samples/incident-data/`,
  five tarballs (the pin lines in the fetch script give each file name and SHA-256).
  Each tarball is one aircraft's extract of OpenSky's Trino tables; the fetch script
  unpacks the position, velocity, identification, ACAS and rollcall-replies tables and the
  README.txt into `opensky/<name>/` (the other tables, allcall, operational status and
  state vectors, stay in the cache). Column names are lower case in three tarballs and
  camelCase in `n722bd` and `xauci`; the tests lower-case the header.
- Licence: CC BY 4.0, stated in each tarball's README ("Cite Schaefer et al. (2014),
  'Bringing up OpenSky'"). Attribution: OpenSky Network, https://opensky-network.org.
  The data is real flights, including two diversions and a fatal accident; do not republish
  derived material without that in mind.
- Content, by file (rows of the unpacked tables; one row per reception, the same frame
  seen by several sensors may be one row with `msgcount` > 1):

  | Name | Aircraft | Window | position | velocity | identification |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `fz1073_2026-09-30_dubai-tabuk` | 8965d1, airliner | 2026-09-30 | 4,798 | 4,466 | 460 |
  | `n722bd_2026-11-01_florida` | a9ab17, Learjet 60 | 2026-11-01 | 12,954 | 8,876 | 1,340 |
  | `n931tt_2026-10-13_wisconsin` | aceb1b, PA-46 | 2026-10-13/14 | 11,801 | 7,676 | 1,178 |
  | `os82_2026-10-18_telaviv-sofia-vienna` | 440604, airliner | 2026-10-18/19 | 25,713 | 20,807 | 2,610 |
  | `xauci_2025-01-31_philadelphia` | 0d086e, Learjet 55 | 2025-01-31 | 22,820 | 20,527 | 1,938 |

- Columns used: `rawmsg` (the frame, hex), `mintime` (receive time, epoch seconds, ms
  resolution), `icao24`; position: `lat`, `lon`, `alt` (metres), `baroalt`, `surface`;
  velocity: `velocity` (m/s), `heading`; identification: `identity` (callsign, space
  padded); ACAS (`*_acas_data4.csv`): `islongformat`, `sensitivitylevel`,
  `replyinformation`, `altitude` (metres), `activeresolutionadvisories` (ARA, 14-bit
  integer), `resolutionadvisorycomplement` (RAC, 4 bits), `hasterminated`,
  `hasmultiplethreats`, `nopassbelow`, `nopassabove`, `noturnleft`, `noturnright`;
  rollcall (`*_rollcall_replies_data4.csv`): `altitude` (metres, DF4/20), `identity` (Mode A
  code, DF5/21). Surface frames are present in `n722bd` (about 470) and `os82` (about 510). No
  DF18 (TIS-B/ADS-R): each file is one aircraft.
- What it exercises: the whole airborne path of the decoder (position, altitude, velocity,
  identification) against another decoder's output for the same frames, in `decode_opensky`
  (`tests/test_decode_opensky.cpp`); the ACAS RA fields, DF0/16 altitude and the rollcall
  altitude and identity, in `decode_acas_opensky` (`tests/test_decode_acas_opensky.cpp`).
  Skipped when absent. OpenSky slices the MV field of every long DF16 as an RA whatever its
  first byte; only 1 of the 2,259 long DF16 frames here has the RA marker 0x30, so the test
  checks the field layout with that byte set to 0x30 in a copy of the frame.
- Not unpacked: the other tables (allcall DF11, operational status, state vectors); they
  stay in the cache tarballs.

## iq/porto-awec2026/ (only with SKYCUE_FETCH_IQ=1)

- Origin: Zenodo record 23342598, "Aircraft radio data - AWEC 2026" (DOI
  10.5281/zenodo.23342598), file `AWEC2026_ADSB_Data.zip` (19,575,669 bytes), unpacked to
  `recording.bin`, `aircraft.csv`, `messages.csv`, `positions.csv`, `candidates.csv`,
  `readme.md` and `license.md` (the `__MACOSX` and `.DS_Store` entries are dropped).
- Licence: CC BY 4.0, Conrado Guimaraes da Costa, University of Porto (license.md).
- Content: `recording.bin`, 72,876,032 bytes, 8-bit unsigned I/Q at 2 MS/s, 18.2 s from
  an RTL-SDR with a 3 m antenna and no LNA, urban; `messages.csv` the 122 frames of one
  aircraft (407181) with decoded fields, `positions.csv` 10 positions, `candidates.csv`
  all 278 demodulator candidates with CRC validity and quality scores.
- Use: a demodulator reference (including CRC-failed candidates); no test reads it yet.
  Not fetched by default to keep the download small (the zip is 20 MB, 73 MB unpacked).
- sha256 of the zip: `407f9d8ebf6451afb7ffa12c768286235f4791fdc8e03fce8136b621108114b9`

## Not used, and why

- Madrid IQ (Zenodo 23360412, CC BY 4.0): 640 MB, 20 s at 8 MS/s; too large to fetch with
  the rest. An opt-in manual download from the record page for demodulator benchmarks;
  not pinned.
- OpenSky's full raw archive (Trino/Impala): needs an account and research terms.
- ADS-B Exchange samples: commercial licence. adsb.lol globe_history: ODbL, decoded
  traces and huge. Zenodo 7923702 and 3937483: non-commercial licences.
- IEEE DataPort recordings: need a login, so no pinned URL.
- EETAC Radarcape days (Zenodo 10054835): decoded SBS text, 150 to 500 MB a day.
- UAT: no public 978 MHz IQ recording was found; the Stratux `example.dump978` and
  `example.radar` uplink-only files carry no timestamps and are not pinned.
